output.content:
Marvell does **not** separately disclose quarterly “electro-optics” revenue within its data-center end market; it reports total data-center revenue, while describing electro-optics/optical interconnects as a product-level driver of that revenue. [[1]] [[2]]

| Fiscal 2026 quarter | Data-center revenue |
|---|---:|
| Q1 | **$1,440.6 million** [[3]]|
| Q2 | **$1,490.5 million** [[2]]|
| Q3 | **$1,517.9 million** [[4]]|
| Q4 | **$1,651.3 million** [[4]]|

The four reported quarters total **$6.1003 billion** in FY2026 data-center revenue, consistent with management’s statement that full-year data-center revenue surpassed $6 billion. [[3]] [[2]] [[4]] [[5]] 

Data-center revenue rose sequentially in every FY2026 quarter—approximately **3.5% in Q2, 1.8% in Q3, and 8.8% in Q4**—with Q4 representing **74%** of Marvell’s total revenue. [[2]] [[4]] 

For electro-optics specifically, management attributed Q1 momentum to “robust shipments” of electro-optics products and said Q2 growth was fueled by AI demand for custom silicon and electro-optics, but it did not quantify electro-optics sales as a stand-alone quarterly revenue line. [[3]] [[2]]
